top_story.headline: House Democrat and Republican team up on a War Powers Resolution over Yemen's Houthis
top_story.dek: Rep. Ro Khanna and Rep. Thomas Massie introduced a resolution to pull U.S. forces out of unauthorized hostilities against the Houthis.
paragraphs: On a day when both chambers met only briefly, the most consequential text introduced was H. Con. Res. 124 from Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), who is joined on the filing by Rep. Thomas Massie. It invokes section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to direct the President to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized.
It was referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs. The Congressional Record shows no floor vote or debate on it on October 9.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions in both chambers; 31 measures introduced in the House
paragraphs: The House met at 12:30 p.m. on Friday, October 9, 2026, with Rep. Erin Houchin presiding as Speaker pro tempore, and adjourned at 12:32 p.m. until 1:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13. The Senate met in pro forma session at 1:30 p.m., adjourned 38 seconds later, and returns at 3:30 p.m. on Tuesday, October 13. No votes were recorded in either chamber, and no Senate bills were listed.

The House Clerk's list of introductions included the Khanna–Massie war powers resolution, a resolution supporting Columbus monuments and a bill to bar federal funds from jurisdictions that celebrate Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day. Every measure introduced is listed below.

items: H.R. 10768, sponsored by Rep. Tom Barrett (R-MI-7) — would create an Office of Artificial Intelligence and Emerging Technology Threats inside the Executive Office of the President.
H.R. 10769, sponsored by Rep. Everton Blair (D-GA-13) — would allow certain facilities within the right-of-way of any Federal-aid highway.
H.R. 10770, sponsored by Rep. Robert Bresnahan (R-PA-8) — would temporarily limit the use of rebates under the 340B drug discount program.
H.R. 10771, sponsored by Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA-2) — would create an emergency preparedness grant program for higher education institutions.
H.R. 10772, sponsored by Rep. Jim Costa (D-CA-21) — would evaluate and invest in Ukrainian defense technologies.
H.R. 10773, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Crank (R-CO-5) — would amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to prevent governmental interference in the operation of private and religious schools.

H.R. 10774, sponsored by Rep. Suzan DelBene (D-WA-1) — would prohibit the taking, importation, exportation and breeding of certain cetaceans (such as whales and dolphins) for public display, amending the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 and the Animal Welfare Act.

H.R. 10775, sponsored by Rep. Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA-10) — would direct the Federal Trade Commission to set up a task force studying the effects of automated accounts on social media, public discourse and elections.
H.R. 10776, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — would change requirements for the allowed take of marine mammals under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972.
H.R. 10777, sponsored by Rep. Pat Fallon (R-TX-4) — would codify certain policies to combat transnational cyber-enabled crime.
H.R. 10778, sponsored by Rep. Valerie Foushee (D-NC-4) — would create a tax credit for health care facilities that use certain low-emission anesthetic gases.
H.R. 10779, sponsored by Rep. Andrew Garbarino (R-NY-2) — would name the Medford, New York, post office at 1905 Route 112 the “Gunnery Sergeant Ruben Santos Post Office Building”.
H.R. 10780, sponsored by Rep. Jared Golden (D-ME-2) — would modify and enhance the federal budgeting and appropriations process.
H.R. 10781, sponsored by Rep. Mike Haridopolos (R-FL-8) — would request that the President designate a month each year as National American History and Founders Month.
H.R. 10782, sponsored by Rep. Jahana Hayes (D-CT-5) — would reauthorize the Clean School Bus Program.
H.R. 10783, sponsored by Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC-1) — would provide for payment of attorney’s fees to a prevailing defendant in a civil defamation or libel action.
H.R. 10784, sponsored by Rep. Richard McCormick (R-GA-7) — would amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide home ownership assistance.
H.R. 10785, sponsored by Rep. Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11) — would reauthorize the SCORE small-business mentoring program under the Small Business Act.
H.R. 10786, sponsored by Rep. Max Miller (R-OH-7) — would require certain institutions to make students who are United States citizens pass the United States naturalization test in order to graduate.
H.R. 10787, sponsored by Rep. Gregory Murphy (R-NC-3) — would exclude urological and ostomy supplies from Medicare competitive acquisition programs for five years.
H.R. 10788, sponsored by Rep. Frank Pallone (D-NJ-6) — the Lower Premiums, Faster Payments Act, which would adjust the surprise medical billing requirements for private health insurance.
H.R. 10789, sponsored by Rep. Jimmy Patronis (R-FL-1) — would establish a moratorium on oil and gas production and exploration in the Eglin Gulf Test and Training Range.

H.R. 10790, sponsored by Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-WA-3) — would require that at least one member of the Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board have demonstrated knowledge and substantial experience in the trades or industrial labor.
H.R. 10791, sponsored by Rep. Michael Rulli (R-OH-6) — would bar federal funds to any state or local government that celebrates Indigenous Peoples Day instead of Columbus Day.
H.R. 10792, sponsored by Rep. Janice Schakowsky (D-IL-9) — would provide incentives for and protect whistleblowers under the authority of the Federal Trade Commission.
H.R. 10793, sponsored by Rep. Derek Schmidt (R-KS-2) — would modify Department of Defense authority for installation support services and intergovernmental support agreements.
H.R. 10794, sponsored by Rep. Norma Torres (D-CA-35) — would create a grant program for states to improve access to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC).

H. Con. Res. 124, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17), with Rep. Thomas Massie — directs the President under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Houthis in Yemen that Congress has not authorized.
H. Res. 1621, sponsored by Rep. J. Luis Correa (D-CA-46) — expresses profound sorrow over the death of Alexander Michel Odeh.
H. Res. 1622, sponsored by Rep. Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24) — expresses support for preserving, protecting and maintaining statues and monuments honoring Christopher Columbus.
H. Res. 1623, sponsored by Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4) — supports recognizing October 2026 as “National Dyslexia Awareness Month.”
